definition: To move is nothing other than to educe something from potency to act. `MovedIn x r`: x is being reduced from potency to act in respect r; `MovesIn y x r`: y so reduces x. Read at one time (simul): a present series of movers, not a history. Nothing restricts it to local motion or to bodies. Aristotle's definition of motion as the actuality of the potential as such, read for beings and respects (STMT-BEING-MOVED-IS-ACTUALIZATION-OF-POTENCY), would make STMT-NOTHING-MOVED-EXCEPT-AS-IN-POTENCY analytic if adopted as the Lean definition of `MovedIn`; it is no stronger than that premise (result ACT-POTENCY-DEFINITIONAL-ANALYSES-CONSERVATIVE), so `MovedIn` stays a parameter.
